protocol.latency: Closed-loop workers. The primary client clock is monotonic perf_counter_ns around payload construction, HTTP, full body read and JSON decode. Server-Timing is reported separately. The four-metric comparison uses pooled request p99, with per-pair p99 and its median alongside. Any HTTP or malformed-response error aborts the measurement; missing samples are never excluded silently. All percentiles use nearest rank. Each series includes whole shuffled passes. Identical dispatch order for both sides in a pair; the second side starts only after the first completes.
protocol.quality: Query-macro averages on the first measured response, counted once per query. Recall/nDCG use graded positives and primary MRR uses queries with exactly one positively graded document; the separate author-target MRR uses designated known-item targets. Verified empty queries are counted separately. Recall ceiling is mean(min(10,n)/n) on positives. The official receipt day is confirmed by the positive qrels; OOD windows are supplied by the author.
protocol.stability: Every ranked list including subsequent warmups is compared with that version's first warm response across all client counts. Each distinct ordered query result is checked for corpus membership, mailbox, as-of date and declared receipt window. Different revisions may return different rankings.
protocol.provenance: Revision labels resolve to local Git commits. The service corpus is checked over HTTP; associating a running service with the intended commit relies on launching that checkout on its declared port.
protocol.privacy: Only aggregates and input file digests are published; no query text, returned IDs or mailbox information.
